title.narrative: UNECE Promoting Innovation in Eastern Europe
UNECE Utveckling av innovationssystem i Östeuropa

description.narrative: The United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) has applied for funding from Sida of 2, 215, 026 USD to carry out the project "Promoting innovation policy capacities in Eastern Europe and the Caucasus" during the period 2018-2022. The intervention aims at improving competencies among innovation policy institutions in designing, running, reforming and monitoring effective innovation policies and institutions. This will be done through (1) the development and regional implementation of an innovation policy index, (2) the cunduct of Innovation Performance Reviews for Sustainable Development in Georgia, Moldova and Armenia and (3) targeted capacity building in Georgia and Moldova and on a regional level.

United Nations Economic Commission for Europe (UNECE) har inkommit med en ansökan till Sida om 2, 215, 026 USD för genomförandet av projektet "Promoting innovation policy capacities in Eastern Europe and the Caucasus" under perioden 2018-2022. Insatsen syftar till stärkt kapacitet hos policyinstitut och beslutsfattare för att skapa, implementera, reformera och underhålla ett funktionellt regelverk och effektiva institutioner för innovation. Detta görs genom (1) utveckling och implementering av ett index för att mäta innovationspolicy, (2) genomförande av studier av nationella innovationssystem (Innovation Performance Reviews for Sustainable Development) i Georgien, Moldavien och Armenien, samt (3) riktade kapacitetsutvecklingsinsatser i bland annat Georgien, Moldavien samt på regional nivå.

"The project will improve the competencies of innovation policy makers in designing, running, reforming, and monitoring effective innovation policies and institutions that make measurable contributions towards long-term economic development and sustainable development." In this programme UNECE focus on Moldova, Armenia and Georgia.
Expected accomplishments EA1.Enhanced capacity of national policy makers and stakeholders to analyse and benchmark their innovation policies and institutions in line with ECE good practices. EA2. Enhanced capacity of national policy makers and stakeholders in three countries to design and carry out effective innovation policy and institutional reform. EA3. Improved subregional cooperation on harmonisation of innovation policies and institutions.
Indicators of achievement IA1.1. At least 3 countries endorsed the findings of the innovation policy index and the I4SD reviews and integrated relevant recommendations into their national policies. IA2.1. At least 80% of stakeholders beneflting from national capacity building confirmed that activities strengthened their capacity in designing, implementing, and evaluating effective innovative policy. IA3.l. At least 5 countries demonstrate that recommendations made in project activities and reflected in the policy handbook are reflected in ongoing or intended changes or reforms to policies, institutions, or instruments.

description.narrative:
Sidas CoP from the latest narrative report by UNECE (24-09-23)
UNECE's innovation report for Eastern Europe and the Caucasus (2023-2024) highlights significant achievements, including:
Enhanced Innovation Policy Capacities: Several countries have embraced the reports recommendations and started integrating these into their national strategies. Armenia, Georgia, and Ukraine expressed strong support and applied the advice to improve their innovation systems.
Capacity Building and Policy Reforms: Ukraine strengthened its innovation policy despite ongoing conflict challenges. UNECE supported this effort through workshops and consultations with relevant stakeholders. Armenia has also initiated a national high-tech strategy following UNECEs recommendations.
idas CoP from the latest narrative report by UNECE (24-09-23)
UNECE's innovation report for Eastern Europe and the Caucasus (2023-2024) highlights significant achievements, including:
Enhanced Innovation Policy Capacities: Several countries have embraced the reports recommendations and started integrating these into their national strategies. Armenia, Georgia, and Ukraine expressed strong support and applied the advice to improve their innovation systems.
Capacity Building and Policy Reforms: Ukraine strengthened its innovation policy despite ongoing conflict challenges. UNECE supported this effort through workshops and consultations with relevant stakeholders. Armenia has also initiated a national high-tech strategy following UNECEs recommendations.
Regional Collaboration and Knowledge Sharing: Initiatives like the Transformative Innovation Network and the Innovation Matters podcast series foster collaboration and knowledge exchange between countries in the region and international experts.
Sidas assessment of the narrative report is UNECE has clearly managed to emphasizes the importance of flexibility, local ownership, and continuous learning when implementing the innovation projects in sensitive areas such as the region.
In 2023, UNECE made significant progress across all work streams, exceeding expectations for the 2022/2023 plan. Notably, UNECE launched the I4SDR (Innovation for Sustainable Development Review) of Ukraine to support its rebuilding and reconstruction efforts. The project received excellent evaluation scores across four categories, though improvements were suggested in integrating the "leave no one behind" principle, prompting UNECE to develop methods for better implementation.
Key achievements include:
Interim Innovation Policy Outlook (IIPO): Building on the 2020 Subregional Innovation Policy Outlook for Eastern Europe and the South Caucasus, UNECE finalized the IIPO in 2022 and officially launched it in 2023. This process included regular meetings with National Focal Points, which facilitated policy exchange and provided input for research.
I4SDR Reviews:
Moldova: The I4SDR of Moldova was launched at a high-level meeting. The review process led to capacity-building activities focused on technology transfer reforms, with UNECE organizing trainings and creating a detailed roadmap for reform. Armenia: The I4SDR review of Armenia, launched in June 2023, explored topics like innovation infrastructure and diaspora investment in agriculture. UNECE is developing a roadmap to support continued reforms, innovation policy, and evidence-based decision-making. National Capacity Building: UNECE led follow-up capacity-building programs in Georgia, Moldova, and Armenia to support domestic reforms based on I4SDR recommendations:
Georgia: UNECE developed a practitioner handbook on innovation-enhancing procurement, organized trainings, and facilitated a study tour to Norway for Georgian officials. Moldova: UNECE provided training and a roadmap for reforming technology transfer initiatives. Armenia: UNECE is preparing a roadmap to strengthen innovation infrastructure and policymaking. National Focal Points Network: UNECE expanded the group of National Focal Points into a larger forum for discussion and best practice exchange. This included regular virtual policy dialogue sessions and the launch of the Innovation Matters podcast series to further engage stakeholders.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
